steps.text: In non-uniform motion the speed keeps changing. Let's compare it with steady motion.
Tap “Start” and watch the object speed up and slow down.
It covers different distances in equal times — sometimes more, sometimes less. That changing speed is non-uniform motion.
Most real motion is like this: a bus speeds up, slows for a stop, then moves again. Its distance-time graph is a curve, not a straight line.

coach.mission: Watch how speed changes in non-uniform motion.
whenStuck: Tap “Start” and watch the object's speed change.
Compare the distance covered in each second.
whenWrong: Non-uniform motion covers unequal distances in equal times — the speed changes.
A changing speed gives a curved distance-time graph.
whenCorrect: Right — the speed keeps changing, so it's non-uniform motion.
Good — unequal steps mean the speed isn't constant.
